passage: The rumour was that I cheated in the unit test. I'm Varun, and I hadn't. Someone started it in a group chat, and by the next morning people were whispering as I walked in. My first instinct was to shout at the whole class. My second was to stay home forever. My chest was tight, and I couldn't eat breakfast. But I sat on the stairs and told myself to breathe. I didn't start a rumour back, though I could think of a few. I told my mother that evening and she came to school with me. I showed my teacher my rough work and the marks list, and posted once in the class chat, "I didn't cheat. My rough work is with the teacher." Nitin sat next to me at lunch the whole week. That helped more than any argument.

qa.q: What was the rumour about Varun?
qa.a: The rumour was that Varun cheated in the unit test.

qa.q: What were Varun's two first instincts, and what was the feeling underneath?
qa.a: Varun wanted to shout at the whole class or stay home forever, and felt afraid: a tight chest and no appetite for breakfast.

qa.q: What did Varun do that helped?
qa.a: Varun calmed down, told their mother, showed the teacher the rough work and the marks list, corrected it once in the chat and did not spread a rumour back.

qa.q: How might Nitin have seen the rumour about Varun?
qa.a: Probably as not worth believing, since Nitin sat next to Varun at lunch the whole week; that steady company said more than any argument.

grounding: A false rumour spreads about Varun; Varun stays calm, tells their mother and the teacher, corrects it once with facts and leans on a real friend.
